items.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
items.q: The name 'Lewis' appears only in the interviewer's turn identifying the location ('Zachary, Lewis, yeah') as a place name (likely a parish or community), with no indication of a personal relationship with the interviewee.

ctx.x: Well, I have met a lot of white folks that really likes the blues. There's a lot of them that I left tapes up there with when I was in Oakland, California. And when I left them overseas, a couple of the white folks, one, well, I left them some tapes. They blew. I said, you want to learn this shit? I said, yes, sit down and take your time. I got to play too fast and I play slow and you learn these blues. And they took them. I give music lessons over there in Oakland. White man that I was staying with, well, he…

Let's see. We're now at Butch Cage's house, huh? Where we at exactly? Zachary, yeah. Zachary, Lewis, yeah. And the number here is? 5131 Old Slaughter Road. 5131 Old Slaughter Road. And what's today's date? It's May the... 13th. 13th. 13th. 13th? May the 13th, 1967. What is your name anyhow? James Cage. And what do they call you? Butch.
How come they call you Butch anyhow? I don't know. Mama called me that nickname.
